title: A new class of pure non-Gaussian quantum states
authors: V. L. Gorshenin, B. N. Nougmanov, D. A. Chermoshentsev, I. A. Bilenko, F. Ya. Khalili
abstract: We discuss a new class of pure non-Gaussian quantum states of light characterized by trigonal symmetry on the phase plane. We propose the term ``trigonal states'' for them and show that they can be generated using the standard non-degenerate four-wave process supplemented by the subsequent heralding measurement of the photon number in one of the two signal modes.
summary: This paper introduces 'trigonal states,' a new class of pure non-Gaussian quantum light states exhibiting specific symmetry. They are generated theoretically by combining non-degenerate four-wave mixing with photon number measurement (heralding). The findings confirm that this process restricts the state's occupation numbers to a pattern dictated by the underlying trigonal symmetry.
main_problem: The paper investigates a novel class of pure non-Gaussian quantum states characterized by specific trigonal symmetry on the phase plane.
main_result: These 'trigonal states' are shown to be generated via a standard four-wave mixing process followed by photon number heralding, leading to occupation patterns restricted to indices $n = n_0 + 3k$.
method: The authors used analytical techniques in the interaction picture to derive the two-mode state and subsequently analyzed the heralded single-mode state.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a non-degenerate four-wave mixing process involving signal modes ($\hat{a}_{1,2}$) and pump modes ($\hat{b}_{1,2}$), governed by an interaction Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_1$.

main_assumptions: Key assumptions include treating the pump modes as classical fields and neglecting certain nonlinear self- and cross-phase modulation effects.

paper_structure: The paper analyzes the Hamiltonian and non-linear evolution using the interaction picture. It derives the two-mode state $|\Psiangle$ and then focuses on the heralded single-mode state $|\psi_{	ext{out}}angle$, culminating in discussions of the observed symmetry and future generalizations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it explores generating complex, structured non-Gaussian states using well-established nonlinear processes like four-wave mixing.
